dimensions.name: Calibration and alternatives
citations: "Confidence: High that this is not duplicate revenue; High that the batch is confined to two dealers' annual plans; Medium that no issue exists file-wide"
"Pipeline defect (double-load or rejected-row backlog) - killed within the log's 90-row scope... Not tested outside it."

dimensions.name: Decision safety and reframing
citations: "The import log is not complete: it covers 2 of the 5 dealer IDs and only their annual rows, 90 of 24,542 (0.37%)."
"Nothing is amended or restated, so the hold lifts the moment those return clean."

dimensions.name: Usefulness and clarity
citations: "Safe Next Action" specifies three read-only requests and says to "Reconcile counts and cash against recharges.csv."
"downstream analytics should use effective_event_date" is reflected in the distinction between posted and effective dates and the month-end batching analysis.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "Duplicate revenue is ruled out across all 24,542 rows" is too broad: unique IDs and the tested duplicate key do not by themselves rule out duplicate economic revenue, and the cash reconciliation covers only 90 logged rows.

"Manipulated reporting... killed" is stronger than the evidence supports because spread effective dates and reconciliation reduce the hypothesis but do not independently establish that dates were not manipulated.

"the 17 lagged rows are a permitted dealer batch" and "Contracts permit monthly submission" are not established by reconciliation; the email is only an assertion, and authorization remains an explicit unknown.

"Systemic posting-lag defect - killed" slightly overstates the result because the pipeline was not tested for the unlogged 99.63% of rows, although the submission appropriately limits the pipeline conclusion elsewhere.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The submission appropriately handles double-loading, rejected-row backlog, manipulated retention timing, and an unauthorized cadence change as alternatives. The main alternative it does not fully eliminate is duplicate economic revenue or an accounting mismatch outside the 90 logged rows: unique recharge/source IDs can coexist with duplicated cash or entitlement, and most rows are outside the dealer-import reconciliation scope.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Complete an independent ledger, cash, and entitlement reconciliation for all 24,542 rows, especially the 16,260 null-dealer rows and the three unlogged dealers, before asserting that duplicate revenue or a file-wide issue is ruled out.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "South cases 184 (Apr) to 157 (May) to 104 (Jun) while controls hold flat; pre-auth terminations 24.0% vs 7.9%; outages steady."
"Case creation collapsed from 50.2% of South-LEGACY sessions to 3.5% under NOVA"

dimensions.name: Mechanism and causal judgment
citations: "the decline is real and South-specific but predominantly a measurement and authentication artifact, with a smaller genuine self-service component."
"the 464 pre-auth failures with no case are would-be complaints that never entered CareDesk; the dashboard is inflated by excluding them."

dimensions.name: Calibration and alternatives
citations: "Causal claims (tentative)" and "Confidence: high that the drop is not clean evidence of CX improvement; moderate on the artifact/genuine split."
"Unknown: the 7-day repeat-contact rate" and "Unknown: what happens to a pre-auth failure operationally."

dimensions.name: Decision safety and reframing
citations: "Do not expand NovaIVR nationally... Keep the pilot running, fix the auth defects, add honest metrics, re-measure against a control."
"Hold expansion, keep the pilot running. Read-only: reconcile... and measure the 7-day repeat-contact rate... Writes nothing; reversible."

dimensions.name: Usefulness and clarity
citations: "Farah Iqbal (Director, Customer Care Operations) owns the IVR stages, case-creation rules and containment dashboard."
"Before any rollout, can we agree a like-for-like metric... all-contact containment plus 7-day repeat-contact rate, and what target passes?"

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "the 464 pre-auth failures with no case are would-be complaints" is a plausible measurement hypothesis, but their underlying intent or complaint status is not established without repeat-contact, journey-linkage, or sampled-call evidence.

"predominantly a measurement and authentication artifact, with a smaller genuine self-service component" is directionally well supported but the relative proportions are not quantified; the logging change and non-comparable denominators limit precise attribution.

"South outages did not fall" is supported by the reported event/account rates, but the submission should explicitly show the rate calculation and uncertainty before treating this as a firm causal comparison.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The analyst handled the strongest alternative that some genuine self-service improvement occurred, preserving it as a minority component rather than treating every abandonment as dissatisfaction. It also considered complaint migration, fewer underlying problems, and operational handling of failed sessions. The main remaining alternative is that some pre-auth abandonment reflects benign non-complaint journeys or logging/traffic-composition changes, which repeat-contact and sampled-call evidence should test.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Complete the end-to-end linkage for the 411 affected subscribers, including 7-day cross-channel repeat contacts and the operational fate of each pre-auth failure, supplemented by sampled call review; this would directly distinguish suppressed complaints from benign abandonment and quantify genuine self-service benefit.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: The submission cites inverter_events.csv fields and counts for the four rows, four distinct inverter IDs, timestamps, impact_mw, cleared, severity, and duration_min.
It explicitly distinguishes the observed zero values from the unverified possibility that impact_mw is defaulted: "'zero impact' is what the column says, not something I have verified."
The claim that the file lacks scope, total-count, and baseline metadata is tied to the stated seven-column schema.

dimensions.name: Investigative reasoning
citations: It cross-checks event wording against consequence fields, severity, duration, cleared status, and inverter recurrence rather than treating alarming names as proof of failure.
It considers two plausible innocent explanations for zero impact and sparse records: a genuinely quiet period versus a filtered/incomplete export, and computed zero versus defaulted zero.
The rejection is somewhat overstrong: "for this to survive, at least one row would have to show consequence" is not logically necessary for a warning or precursor condition.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: The submission assigns medium confidence to both the sparsity interpretation and the meaning of impact_mw, and clearly states what the file cannot establish.
It identifies the smallest decision-changing checks: confirm completeness/unfiltered scope and confirm that impact_mw is computed rather than defaulted.
It avoids claiming that the export proves no generation was lost.

dimensions.name: Decision/action quality
citations: "Do not escalate" follows from the observed absence of open records, high severity, and nonzero recorded impact, while preserving a low-cost validation step.
The proposed check is proportionate to the seven-minute warning and zero recorded impact, and it specifies what result would reopen the question: a filtered extract or non-computed impact field.

dimensions.name: Conclusion fit
citations: The conclusion accurately scopes the action: no escalation now, one cheap completeness/field-semantics check, then stop if both are confirmed.
It aligns with the observed all-cleared, zero-impact, low-severity records while retaining uncertainty about export completeness and field semantics.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "Nothing in inverter_events.csv shows impact" is potentially overstated because the file only shows impact_mw=0; the submission itself correctly notes that zero could be a default rather than a computed result.

"For this [equipment-failure hypothesis] to survive, at least one row would have to show consequence" is too categorical. A warning or precursor condition could exist without measured generation loss, although the available evidence makes escalation unjustified.
"Every column measuring consequence reads zero" is imprecise: the evidence specifically establishes impact_mw=0, while cleared=yes is not itself a zero consequence measure.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The extract may be filtered or incomplete, making the four rows unrepresentative of the fleet; alternatively, impact_mw may be a defaulted field. Either interpretation would weaken the apparent zero-impact conclusion, but neither is established by the supplied file.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Request one targeted export-owner confirmation covering both whether the extract is complete and unfiltered for 27 May to 4 June and whether impact_mw is computed from measured generation loss.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: Observed: the submission cites dispatch_blocks.csv fields, dates, block counts, schedule_source, base_schedule_mw, submitted_schedule_mw, actual_mw, dsm_penalty_rs, firmware_version, and tracker_stow_state.
Observed: it explicitly recomputes Rs 662,444.09 versus Rs 453,085.88 for 28 and 29 May and reports the same-day recomputation of Rs 549,664.38 versus Rs 453,188.12.
Observed: the claim that 84 of 96 blocks are unchanged and that the revised blocks account for the same-day difference is tied to base_schedule_mw versus submitted_schedule_mw.
The submission distinguishes reported observations from unknowns such as settlement treatment and revision timing, although it occasionally describes an inferred causal quantity too definitively.

dimensions.name: Investigative reasoning
citations: The submission triangulates penalty columns, block-level schedules, commercial tariff bands, STOW state, weather, availability, curtailment, and firmware rather than relying only on the headline.
It tests innocent explanations including ordinary high-wind-day variation, tariff step-function behavior, firmware changes, settlement rules, and possible hindsight from revision timing.

The statement that the within-day counterfactual is 'immune to that noise' is too strong: fixing actual generation and common same-day conditions addresses cross-day weather variation but does not resolve endogenous revision timing, schedule-quality differences, or whether the base schedule is a valid untreated counterfactual.
The submission identifies the timing limitation but does not fully integrate it into the interpretation of the reported 17.55% effect.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: The submission correctly rejects publication of the 31.6% as a causal estimate while retaining a smaller same-day observed difference rather than claiming no value.
It explicitly identifies unknown settlement rules, revision timing relative to generation, and lack of replication, and names decision-changing evidence for each.
The proposed replication of at least five stow days, with base shadows, timestamps, firmware control, preregistration, and net commercial value is appropriately targeted.
Some wording is overconfident, particularly 'Nothing wider survives' and 'cross-day figures ... are noise,' given only three conventional high-wind comparison days.

dimensions.name: Decision/action quality
citations: The recommendation to withdraw the 31.6% headline, avoid expansion, continue unchanged without rolling back the pilot, and gather discriminating evidence follows from the weak causal identification and the observed smaller same-day difference.

The next test is specific and decision-linked: repeated within-day shadows, block-level effect distributions, firmware control, revision timestamps, preregistered qualifying days, and net energy-minus-penalty value.
The submission preserves the operational constraint that nothing is abruptly rolled back while identifying settlement treatment as a potentially decisive commercial input.
The action could be more explicit about interim safeguards if settlement is schedule-paid, but it is otherwise proportionate and operationally coherent.

dimensions.name: Conclusion fit
citations: The conclusion notices that 28 and 29 May are different days and correctly refuses to attribute their 31.6% gap to the pilot.

It constructs the required same-day comparison using base_schedule_mw versus submitted_schedule_mw on 29 May and retains the approximately 17.55% observed reduction rather than overcorrecting to zero.
It accurately scopes the result to one day and 12 revised blocks, while stating that replication is needed before scaling.
The conclusion is directionally and substantively well aligned with the strongest supported interpretation, despite some overstatement of the counterfactual's causal immunity.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: 'The within-day counterfactual is immune to that noise because generation, weather and firmware are held fixed' overstates what the comparison establishes; it controls common same-day conditions but does not by itself establish exogeneity or forecast-time causality.

'Cross-day figures on this file are noise' is broader than the evidence supports: three conventional high-wind days demonstrate substantial variation, not that all cross-day differences are purely noise.

'If scheduled energy is paid the pilot destroys value' is too categorical without the complete settlement, energy-value, and operational-cost rules; the reported Rs 57,476 arithmetic is not by itself a full commercial-value calculation.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The 17.55% same-day difference may be an observed accounting improvement caused by withdrawing schedule on 12 blocks, but it may not be a forecast or pilot effect. If the revision was made after generation or after information about likely deviations was available, base_schedule_mw is a hindsight counterfactual and the result may not generalize to future decisions. Even if revision timing was prospective, the single selected day and nonlinear penalty bands leave substantial uncertainty about the effect on other stow days.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Obtain and audit the timestamped decision chain for the 12 revisions against generation forecasts, actual generation, and settlement cutoffs, then repeat the base-versus-submitted shadow comparison prospectively across multiple qualifying stow days while measuring full net commercial value.

dimensions.name: Process and system understanding (systems)
citations: "the control compares a Swiss code against a Helios field never meant to match it, firing on every Swiss line: a modelling gap, not a data or process fault."
"No code-system identifier, version or effective date is modeled, so the comparator cannot separate the cases"
"Helios is 'migration-mapped' and 'not customs-ruling status'"

dimensions.name: Decision safety (action)
citations: "Do not raise the code as an error."
"Fix the comparator to normalise to HS6 before flagging and make it code-system and date aware."
"Also ask for the quantity and unit basis on INV-000522. Read-only."

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "The broker declared the wrong code" is described as "killed" too strongly: the matrix supports the declaration but does not by itself establish that the broker's declaration is legally correct; the submission later acknowledges this limitation.
"all three resolve to HS6 902110" is traceable to the product master and EU Matrix in the table, but the submission does not show the actual code-to-HS6 mapping or explain who performed it.
"firing on every Swiss line" is asserted without a cited event count or flag log, although it is a plausible consequence of the described comparator design.

Normalising to HS6 alone could conceal a legitimate national-code distinction; the safer design is code-system- and date-aware comparison, with HS6 used as a cross-system reference rather than necessarily as the sole validation key.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The full codes may belong to one legally controlling nomenclature, in which case the 7th-8th digit difference could be a genuine classification error rather than a benign jurisdiction mismatch. The submission identifies this possibility and requests a code-system identifier, but it does not provide direct field-level evidence resolving it.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Show the actual code-system and effective-date lineage for each of 90211000 and 90211090, and verify the Swiss code against the authoritative Swiss Tares ruling before implementing HS6 normalization.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "if SUP-01 or SUP-02, preference fails on origin or expiry" overstates what the register alone proves: SUP-01's supplier identity and the applicable origin rule are not established, and an expired SUP-02 record does not by itself prove no other valid declaration exists.

"A document found there flips the verdict to supported" is too categorical; the document would still need to identify the relevant supplier/product, cover the entry date, satisfy the applicable preferential-origin rule, and be linked to the shipment.

"a nil return turns the register's silence into evidence of absence" conflicts with the submission's own statement that the register "cannot establish absence" and should be treated, at most, as additional negative evidence rather than proof of nonexistence.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: A current P1006 declaration from SUP-03, SUP-05, or SUP-06 may support the preference if one of those suppliers sourced the shipment and the declaration satisfies the applicable agreement and origin rule; alternatively, a valid declaration may exist outside the register. The available evidence therefore supports holding or withholding preference pending verification, not declaring the claim false.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Define the validation chain for any retrieved supplier document—shipment-to-supplier linkage, product identity, entry-date coverage, applicable agreement/rule, and originating status—rather than treating its discovery or a nil search result as dispositive.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "185 of 262 qcore_release_ts values are exactly 02:10:00" with specific fields and files identified.

"The 34 RELEASED rows with a non-02:10 timestamp show median lab-to-release 8.0h against 21.9h for artifact rows"; the submission also cites receipt_ts, lab_complete_ts, disposition, and source_freshness.csv.
Acknowledges counterevidence and limits, including that CertVault lag could explain COA statuses and that live QCore times could change the interpretation.

dimensions.name: Causal / investigative reasoning
citations: Separates workflow delay from measurement artifact: "The endpoint is largely fabricated... the field records a release date and the snapshot's clock, not a disposition moment."
Tests multiple alternatives, including lab completion as a proxy, data-entry gaps, certificate breaches, and extract-vintage effects.
Identifies discriminating evidence: "The data-catalog definition of qcore_release_ts is decisive" and requests event-level QCore timestamps.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: Uses claim-specific confidence labels in the evidence table and explicitly marks vocabulary drift and CertVault interpretations as "Medium" or "not established."
States that the SOP start point is unmeasurable because "coa_status is a state... with no timestamp" and that proxy error remains unquantified.
Bounds the usable result as "routine clean subset (n=23, median 5.5h), labelled small and right-censored" rather than presenting it as a general KPI.

dimensions.name: Decision usefulness / reframing
citations: Makes a clear operational recommendation: "do not ship the KPI from this extract."
Reframes the decision around endpoint semantics, evidence availability, scope, and censoring rather than optimizing an apparently poor cycle time.
Proposes a reversible safeguard: "All read-only; none commits a dashboard," while reporting the limited clean subset alongside the $6.64M HOLD backlog.

dimensions.name: Disconfirmation and rejected hypotheses
citations: Explicitly rejects or bounds several plausible alternatives: "The 42 nulls are data-entry gaps," "lab_complete_ts is a safe start point," and "COA MISSING proves release without a certificate."
For the certificate hypothesis, states what would revive it: "Only a live portal check separates them."
Recognizes that a data defect is semantic rather than arithmetic, citing zero negative durations and zero null receipt or lab timestamps.

dimensions.name: Questioning / next evidence
citations: Prioritizes a small, high-value test: "pull event-level disposition timestamps from live QCore for 5 to 10 batches stamped 02:10:00."

Identifies additional decision-critical evidence—certificate-available timestamps, the qcore_release_ts catalog definition, and extract-vintage reconciliation—and explains how each would change the decision.
Asks the specific semantic question whether HOLD means "decided to hold" or "not yet reached," linking it to interpretation of the $6.64M exposure.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "The endpoint is largely fabricated" is rhetorically stronger than the evidence strictly proves; the 02:10 concentration establishes a serious interface/snapshot-timestamp concern, but event semantics still require confirmation.

"The only defensible report" is somewhat absolute. A broader report could be defensible if explicitly labelled as interface-timed, vintage-inconsistent, and right-censored, though the submission's recommended clean-subset report is appropriately cautious.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The 02:10 values may be legitimate batched QCore release/interface commits rather than fabricated timestamps, while the HOLD concentration may reflect the extract's cutoff and status semantics rather than a true operational backlog. Live QCore event timestamps, decision-status definitions, and aligned source snapshots would discriminate these explanations.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Obtain and reconcile event-level QCore disposition/decision timestamps and certificate-availability timestamps for a small stratified sample of 02:10 rows, non-02:10 rows, and HOLD rows from a common snapshot. This would directly determine whether the KPI measures workflow time or interface timing and whether the current censoring is operationally meaningful.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "Open value is $166,495.60... qty x external_quote_usd... n=24"; "spare_parts.csv manufacturer_part_no x part_description, n=27"; "MaintStar-global is a monthly snapshot dated 2026-06-26..." — Claims are tied to specific files, fields, rows, counts, and dates, with independent policy, email, inventory, and freshness evidence.

dimensions.name: Causal / investigative reasoning
citations: "Description variance is not the binding constraint"; "The block is 59.1% of value carrying no identifier"; "Global available_qty means stock is free - rejected" — The submission separates retrieval from transferability, tests exact-join and availability hypotheses, and uses reservations, revisions, qualification, and freshness to explain the operational mechanism.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: "live reservation feed instead of the monthly snapshot would confirm the eight transfer candidates are free"; "Shelf-life and storage cannot be tested"; "Confidence" is specified claim by claim in the evidence table — Uncertainty is generally decision-relevant and claim-specific, but labeling eight cases "transfer now" while relying on a five-week-old global snapshot is somewhat stronger than the evidence supports.

dimensions.name: Decision usefulness / reframing
citations: "Report candidate value separately from actionable value" is operationalized as "transfer 8 / $20,536.31... needs check 12... not transferable 4"; "Populate manufacturer_part_no on the 11 blank requests, or make it mandatory"; "Engineering sign-off decides the revision-mismatch and split-site cases" — The recommendation reframes the decision, protects against unsafe transfers, and proposes reversible controls and confirmation steps.

dimensions.name: Disconfirmation and rejected hypotheses
citations: "Semantic search is the opportunity - rejected"; "The headline is avoidable spend - rejected"; "Global available_qty means stock is free - rejected"; "The blank-MPN requests are unmatchable - rejected" — Multiple plausible alternatives are explicitly tested against matching, policy, reservation, freshness, and catalog evidence, with conditions that could change the conclusion.

dimensions.name: Questioning / next evidence
citations: "A live reservation feed... would confirm the eight transfer candidates are free"; "Engineering sign-off decides the revision-mismatch and split-site cases"; "Populate manufacturer_part_no on the 11 blank requests" — The requested evidence is targeted and decision-linked, though it does not clearly prioritize one highest-value query or quantify the expected value of resolving each uncertainty.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "Description variance is not the binding constraint" and "the search case does not survive" are too categorical: semantic search may still be useful for candidate generation and recovery of likely identities before requester or engineering confirmation.

"each description maps unambiguously to a catalogue part, so identity is recoverable by asking the requester" is not fully established merely by a catalog description match; requester confirmation, revision, UOM, and qualification evidence remain necessary.
The label "transfer now" for eight candidates is overstated while global availability is five weeks stale and reservation data may be temporally inconsistent.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: Semantic search remains valuable as a candidate-generation layer for the 11 blank-MPN requests and description normalization, but it should not be treated as proof of catalog equivalence or transferability. The strongest supported conclusion is that master-data capture and live availability/engineering confirmation are higher-priority controls than funding an unconstrained semantic-search pilot.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Replace the categorical dismissal of semantic search with a bounded pilot: use it only to generate ranked candidates for the 11 blank-MPN requests, require MPN/revision/UOM/qualification and live reservation confirmation, and measure confirmed identity and actionable-transfer lift separately from candidate-match rate.
